topics.title: Non-fiction and Shaw's idea of a perfectly free person

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the forms and purpose of non-fiction writing as described in the section introduction.
Explain why Shaw holds that no person can be perfectly free because of natural necessities.

topics.title: Natural slavery and the slavery of man to man
topics.ncert_sections: Freedom (G.B. Shaw), on stolen labour, governments and Nature

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how, according to Shaw, one class shifts its share of labour on to another.
Interpret Shaw's criticism of governments, elections and the vote.
Distinguish the pleasant slavery to Nature from the hateful slavery of man to man.

topics.title: The humbug of freedom and the delusion of the master class
topics.ncert_sections: Freedom (G.B. Shaw), on propaganda, the gentleman and human nature

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the historical events that people are taught to see as victories for freedom.
Explain why Shaw thinks the master class is more deluded than the enslaved masses.
Evaluate the two views Shaw presents on whether human nature can be changed.

topics.title: Restrictions on freedom and freedom as leisure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ways in which laws, landlords and employers restrict individual freedom.
Explain Shaw's view of the strike and the general strike.
Interpret Shaw's advice to call freedom leisure and to work out how much of it a worker has.
Explain why Krishnamurti considers discipline and freedom contradictory.
Analyse how conformity to tradition prevents the growth of intelligence.
Explain how fear and self-concern destroy sensitivity.

topics.title: Language work: sentence types, rhetorical questions and sound sequences

concepts.learning_objective: Classify sentences as simple, complex or compound and identify main clauses.
Infer the implied statement behind a rhetorical question.
Write the consonant-vowel sound sequence of a word.
